subject: ADR-208: a silent button is not an output -- and the rule that decided what a button is was a check about spelling
body: The audit that exists to find work a page CANNOT HAND OVER decided what a BUTTON was from the word `save` in a label and from whether a control's kind was spelt ending in `_in`. Every control on every page has a label, so that regex alone would press half a page, and the line that was supposed to stop it -- kind.endswith("_in") -- IS A CHECK ABOUT HOW A KIND IS SPELT: it catches text_in, field_in and file_in, and lets step_val, slider, select, checkbox, drop_zone, pick_opt and tab straight through, which is most of what this kit composes. verify_outputs pinned that rule with an <input>, THE ONE KIND WHOSE SPELLING HAPPENS TO MATCH, and it read green for fifty-five slices. So a number box captioned 'Plants you plan to save seed from' was pressed as an export, handed nothing over, and was filed `silent`. What a button IS, is now read from the door's own `activate` argument pool -- a control the door does not press cannot hand anything over -- which is ADR-141's rule for the fifth time in five slices. WHAT MADE IT INVISIBLE is the other half: SILENT WAS A NUMBER IN A COLUMN, named nowhere, held by no ratchet, and never the reason for a non-zero exit, so an export that quietly stopped working, a control that should never have been pressed, and a page that is right to hand nothing over all read identically. Silence is a second worklist with a second ratchet now -- mute_ceiling, per page, may not rise, comes down as buttons are fixed -- and a button that is right to be silent is DECLARED WITH A REASON stored word for word. EIGHTEEN READINGS BECAME NINE REAL ONES, all nine declared: Save to collection / Save to cross / Save this run commit a row to the page's own list and are entry, not handover; 'Choose .eco file...', 'import these .eco lines' and 'Controller export' are the other direction entirely; track-eco is a pane chooser; and fkq/'no print / not applicable' is a key answer about a SPORE PRINT, the deposit a cap leaves on paper overnight. THE FALSE CANDIDATE WAS HIDING A TRUE TRAP: the breeding bench takes eighteen typed values across a roguing log and a replicated yield trial with no way to get any of it off the screen, and ADR-205's rule -- a page with NO output button is the loudest row a ledger can print -- never fired, because the page had one. It exports now (Copy the bench sheet, Download bench.csv, one section per table, with the population and selection figures beside the rows they were read against, and an outbox ledger); so does the CP BENCH, which could hand over a soil recipe and nothing else and now hands over its water log, mix, plants, observations, dormancy record and crosses; and so does the ECOLOGY LAB, which BUILT the protocol a student is told to save and left it in a read-only textarea, where selecting 120px of text by hand on a phone is where the morning is lost. Both benches were named as unfixed in ADR-207 section 4; both are fixed here. EVERY NEW EXPORT IS HELD -- the page's own task presses it and asks what came out, against the rows that task entered. A REFUSAL NOBODY ASKED FOR IS A FAILURE, and this slice's own first draft is the evidence: it wrote collect-output with a `selector` that action does not take, the door refused both bench tasks' steps, and each reported PASS with 115 confirmed and the one step whose whole job was to read the export never run. A step that FAILED with nothing said about it has ended the task since ADR-126; a step the door REFUSED graded nothing, because it expected nothing, and the runner moved on. The kit already had the grammar -- expect {ok:false}, or an expectation about `code`, which is what the collection sheet's hostgone uses -- so the rule reads off WHAT THE TASK CLAIMED rather than a list of steps allowed to be refused, which would go stale the first time a task grew one. All 55 shipped tasks still hold. NO TARGET IN THIS KIT ANSWERS A STEP WITH A DECLINE -- the fixture's destructive rung answers `failed`, the other branch -- so that half of the rule has no violator anywhere and is driven through a SCRIPTED DOOR that answers exactly the way a declining gateway does: ADR-207's finding arriving on the rule written to answer ADR-207's finding. A MUTANT SURVIVED the first draft of the mute ratchet's direction check for the same reason, because it was written from a reading that already equalled the ceiling; rewritten from a page that is OVER its ceiling. AND THE LEDGER IS MARKED FROM TWO PLACES: the outbox suite read a page's copyText call sites, and a DOWNLOAD has no clipboard promise to hang the mark on, so the page calls .sent(id, bytes) itself in the path where the bytes went -- both new downloads were reported as exports declared and impossible, the rule enforced over one of the two shapes the thing it measures actually has. It reads both now -- and THE DOWNLOADS THEMSELVES ARE NOT MARKED, because a hosted viewer refuses a page-started download SILENTLY, with no throw and no return value, so a mark beside a.click() would be ADR-203's defect one layer along: the ledger reporting a sheet as gone from this device that the browser never let leave. The copy is declared and marked, the download carries the sentence the experiment guide already carries, and the .sent reader -- now with no violator in the kit -- is driven over a source written in the suite, both shapes in one line plus the component's own forwarding call that must not count. ONE MORE THE FULL RUN FOUND: the ecology lab's new copy status line was written under a name outside read-report's convention, so audit_readable reported a figure the harness cannot see the day it appeared -- which is that ratchet working; renamed rather than declared furniture, because the outcome of a copy is worth reading. verify_outputs 38 -> 58, mutate_outputs 31 -> 44 all killed, verify_tasks 383 -> 392, mutate_tasks 87 -> 91 all killed, verify_outbox 316 -> 337. 0 of 80 outputs leave a page with nothing reading them, 0 buttons hand over nothing that has not been judged in writing, and twenty-four pages carry a mute ceiling of zero.
